inner.headline: Aeration dates.
inner.body: When, which greens, and for how long.

inner.headline: Holiday hours.
inner.body: Dining, the golf shop and the fitness center, each on its own schedule.

inner.headline: The winter dining schedule.
inner.body: Which nights, which rooms, and when it starts.

reveal.detail: Members ask about what is new. The answers a club publishes have to be just as new.

close.headline: Review the club's published hours and policies each time the season turns.
close.body: An assistant is only as current as what the club gives it.
close.tryBody: Ask members which fall change they want to hear about first.

caption:
Every club's calendar rewrites its most common questions a few times a year. Aeration week brings one set. Holiday hours bring another. The first cold morning brings questions about frost and course openings.

The pattern is simple: members ask about whatever changed last. That only works in the club's favor if the published answer changed too.

What is the first question your members start asking this time of year?
firstComment: Spring brings its own list. It is worth writing down before the first warm weekend.

earnsItsPlace: Ties seasonal operations to keeping the club's published answers current, which is what Club Pilot's assistant answers from; a generic golf account would post the season without the operational point.
